_comment: Motive-based recruitment. Each person weighs their own motives (0..1 weights from who they are); an offer satisfies some of them. They accept when the weighted total reaches 'threshold'; one strong motive met in full can be enough on its own. Close calls get a counteroffer; refusals say why in plain words. Offers are real: wages come from the treasury every day, homes are moved into, jobs need a workplace, and promises are checked.
_renegotiate: New terms for a retainer: taken if they're no worse (by the retainer's own motives) than 'tolerance' below the old ones; loyalty rises by the gain x loyalty_per_gain (up to max_loyalty); turned-down worse terms cost refused_loyalty.
_strong_motive: A motive whose weight x satisfaction reaches 'weight' counts 'bonus' times over: one strong reason can be enough.

bond.name: Fondness for you
bond._: satisfied by their opinion of you; loyal and kind people weigh it more

money.name: Money and security
money._: satisfied by a daily wage against what they need

home.name: A home for their family
home._: satisfied by a better home (or a promise of one)

career.name: Advancement
career._: training, an office, a workplace with tools, or a squire's path

standing.name: Respect, duty and prestige
standing._: an appeal to duty, an office or a title

ties.name: Ties to their life here
ties._: a cost: their business, friends and family keep them

risk.name: Caution
risk._: a cost: craven or content people dislike change

_trade: Skilled trades: joining your house means giving up the trade, unless you offer a workplace where they can keep it.
_wage_need: Gold a day they need; a gifted hand knows their worth (best current ability at or above each step adds 1).
_livelihood: People who live by their work give up their living to join: no wage at all counts against the offer.
_heir_ties: Their own bond with the heir: friends and lovers count for more, rivals for less.

training.name: Training in a skill of their choosing

squire.name: A squire's place, on the road to knighthood

bond: "Your family has always been fair to mine, {lord}."
"I'd follow you, {lord}. I've said so before."
money: "Truth be told, {lord}, we owe the miller more than we can pay."
"A steady wage... that would change everything for us."
home: "Five of us under one roof, and the roof leaks."
"If my children had a proper home, I'd go anywhere."
career: "I'm wasted here. I could do so much more, if someone gave me the chance."
"Teach me, {lord}, and you won't regret it."
standing: "My family has served this village for generations. That should count for something."
"Money is nothing. A man's name, his duty, that is something."
ties: "My whole life is here, {lord}. My work, my friends."
"Who would keep the business going if I left?"
risk: "I don't like changes, {lord}. Things are fine as they are."
